column1: # Where each Old English noun's gender in lex-ang.tsv was read.
# The tooltip prints a noun's gender beside it, and its word page prints it
# in the Gender row and the page's description. On 2026-10-04 every noun was
# read against English Wiktionary's Old English entry, and against
# Bosworth–Toller, the dictionary the pack's attribution names, wherever
# Wiktionary has no entry for the word, disagrees with itself, or disagrees
# with the seed. One was wrong: wīfmann, woman, was marked feminine, and is
# "wíf-mann … es; m. (but seó wífman occurs)" — declined as mann is, of
# which it is a compound (Sievers tr. Cook §281 note 1; Wright's Elementary
# A Wiktionary page holds every word of one spelling, so a line citing it
# means the gender of this word's own etymology there: stefn, voice, is
# feminine where stefn, stem, is masculine, and lagu, law, a loan from
# Norse, is feminine where lagu, sea, is masculine. Where Wiktionary gives two
# genders for one word (lēo, rūm, setl, clāð, heofon, sǣ, hyll, friþ), the
# Where Wiktionary was not enough, Bosworth–Toller decided: hīwsċipe,
# onsīen (an-sýn), pæð and blis have no Wiktionary entry under those titles;
# īren's Wiktionary header says masculine and its own declension table a
# neuter a-stem, and Bosworth–Toller has "íren, es; n."; þorp is neuter in
# Wiktionary and "þorp, þrop, es; m." in Bosworth–Toller. ċildclāð, which
# the pack taught for "baby" until 2026-10-07, was neuter in the main
# dictionary and "m. (not n.)" in its Supplement; it is a swaddling-cloth,
# and "baby" is ċild now. fremde is an adjective, used as a noun for a
# stranger, and Wiktionary gives that sense; masculine, as of a man.
# Each line names the entries it was read in, separated by spaces:
#                      (the title drops macrons and the dots of ċ and ġ)
# tests/tools/genders.test.ts requires every noun in lex-ang.tsv to have a
# line here giving the same gender, every line to name an entry — a
# Wiktionary one being the word's own — and no line to outlive its noun. It
# cannot tell an entry somebody read from one somebody typed.
